questions.prompt: Why does a tool-call-delta chunk carry an index?
options: To count how many tool calls the model has made in the session
Because pieces of two tool calls requested at once can arrive interleaved
Because tool calls must be run in index order
To tell the provider which tool schema was used
questions.explanation: When the model asks for several tools in one reply, their pieces can be mixed together in the stream. The index says which call each piece belongs to.

questions.prompt: translate sees finish_reason: 'tool_calls' on a data line. Why doesn't it emit the finish chunk right away?
options: Usage may still arrive, and nothing may come after finish
The finish chunk must wait until the tool has run
DeepSeek sends finish_reason more than once per reply
The reason must first be checked against the tool schema
questions.explanation: The rule is usage before finish and nothing after it. The translator remembers the reason and emits finish only at [DONE], once usage has been passed on.

questions.prompt: Why are tool-call arguments kept as raw string fragments in chunks, rather than parsed objects?
options: Parsing JSON is too slow to do while streaming
The model sends arguments in a format that is not JSON
A fragment such as {"pa is only part of a JSON object and cannot be parsed yet
The rest of the program never needs the arguments
questions.explanation: Arguments arrive a few characters at a time. Until all the pieces are joined, the text is not a complete JSON object, so it stays a string.
